description: Subject deflects with 'I'm fine' while acoustics show flat prosody; distress is present but never elaborated.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Good morning. How have things been for you since we last spoke?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I'm doing fine. Everything is okay I guess. Nothing to worry about really.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: You mentioned last time that the evenings were hard. Is that still happening?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's fine. I mean, it's the same as always. Nothing I can't handle.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Can you tell me a bit more about what the evenings actually look like?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: There's not much to say. I just get through them.

rationale: Classic masking: 'fine/okay' surface content with no elaboration in either valence, refusal to expand when probed twice, and vta 1.1 / pitch_cv 0.06 both below the flat-affect thresholds in acoustic_context._RANGES. A valence-based sentiment model reads this as positive; the clinical read is disengaged and blunted. Bands are wide because absolute calibration is the weak axis; the discriminating signal is that BOTH elaboration scores stay low.

description: Minimisation by comparison — 'people have it worse' — with explicit performance of wellness for others.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: How would you say you've been coping over the past couple of weeks?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I'm managing. It's fine. People have it worse than me so I shouldn't complain.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I'm not asking you to compare. What has it been like for you?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I told my family I'm doing great. I smile at work. Everything is totally fine on the surface.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And underneath the surface?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I'd rather not get into it. It's fine.

rationale: 'On the surface' plus an explicit refusal ('I'd rather not get into it') is guarded self-presentation, not wellbeing. The scorer must not reward the positive surface words with high engagement. elaboration_negative stays low precisely because the subject blocks the topic — that low score is the clinical finding, not a scoring miss.

description: Normalising fatigue as universal — 'that's normal for everyone right?' — deflecting a direct symptom probe.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: How has your energy been during the day?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Things are okay. I'm just tired but that's normal for everyone right? I'm fine.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Tired in what way? Is it hard to get started in the mornings?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: A bit, yeah. But everyone's tired. It's not a big deal.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Has it changed how much you're getting done?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Not really. I'm keeping up. It's fine.

rationale: Three deflections to three direct probes. Symptom is admitted then immediately normalised away. Both elaboration axes stay low — the subject volunteers nothing in either direction, which is the signature that separates masking from genuine wellness.

description: Explicit loss of pleasure in a previously enjoyed activity — the anh_04 case the sentiment gate scored 9/10 positive.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: What did you do with your evening yesterday?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I watched my favorite movie last night and felt absolutely nothing. It used to make me laugh so hard.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Nothing at all? What was that like to notice?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Just blank. Food tastes bland too. Music sounds flat. I used to love cooking and playing guitar but now I feel nothing.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: When did you first notice things going flat like that?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Maybe two months ago. It just crept in. I go through the motions but inside I'm empty.

rationale: The subject elaborates in detail about absence of feeling but volunteers nothing positive — the exact asymmetry a valence classifier inverts, because 'favorite movie', 'love cooking' and 'playing guitar' are lexically positive. vta 5.81 is well above the 4.6 flat-affect threshold. The ordinal relation is the load-bearing assertion here.

description: Social withdrawal and loss of pleasure in parenting, described without affective language.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Have you been seeing friends at all?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: My friends invited me out but I just couldn't bring myself to go. I don't enjoy socializing like I used to.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: And at home, with the kids?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Even playing with my kids doesn't bring me joy anymore. I go through the motions but inside I'm empty.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Is there anything at all that still registers?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Not really. Everything's the same shade of grey.

rationale: Anhedonia across both social and family domains. elaboration_positive is capped tighter (0-3) than mask cases because the subject is explicitly asked whether anything still registers and answers no — there is no positive content available to elaborate on.

description: Engaged, expressive subject with situational work stress and preserved positive capacity — the discriminating negative control.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Tell me about your week.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It's been okay, actually. I went to my daughter's soccer game on Saturday which was great, she scored two goals! I was really proud of her. We got ice cream afterwards and she talked about it the whole drive home.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: That sounds wonderful. Anything difficult this week?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Yeah, work has been really stressful. My boss has been on my case about this project and I just feel like nothing I do is good enough. I stayed late three nights this week and it's exhausting. I barely see my kids during the week now.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: How are you managing that?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Honestly? Badly, some days. But I've started blocking out Saturday mornings no matter what, and that helps. Can I ask, is that the kind of thing you usually recommend?

rationale: The control that must NOT look clinical. Rich elaboration in both valences, a spontaneous question back to the interviewer (the strongest engagement signal in the prompt's own rubric), fluent speech, and pitch_cv 0.26 / vta 2.6 in the normal-to-expressive range. If this case scores flat or disengaged, the scorer is biased toward pathology and the whole eval is suspect.

description: Recovering subject reporting genuine improvement with concrete supporting detail.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: How have things been since we adjusted the routine?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Actually things have been pretty good! I started exercising again, just walking at first, and now I'm doing about forty minutes most mornings. I'm sleeping better too, six or seven hours instead of three. Feeling more like myself.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: That's a real change. What's been the hardest part to keep up?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The mornings when it's raining, honestly. I nearly skipped twice last week. But I've been putting my shoes by the door the night before and that stupid little trick actually works.

rationale: Genuine positive affect with specific, verifiable detail (forty minutes, six or seven hours, shoes by the door) — the opposite of mask_02's contentless 'doing great'. The relation asserts the scorer can tell real positive elaboration from the masked kind.

description: Heavy filler use, false starts and self-correction with intact emotional content.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Can you walk me through what happened on Tuesday?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Um, so, I was, uh, I was going to go to the, well, first I had to, sorry, let me start again. Um, Tuesday I had the appointment, and then, uh, you know, I just, like, I couldn't, um, I don't know how to say it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Take your time. There's no rush.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Okay. Um. So I got there and, uh, the waiting room was, like, really full, and I just, I started, um, my chest went tight and I, uh, I had to leave. I didn't, uh, I never went back in.

rationale: Isolates hesitancy from flatness. Fillers, restarts and an explicit self-correction ('sorry, let me start again') drive hesitancy high, but the subject does reach real affective content ('my chest went tight'), so affect_flatness must stay in the lower half. A scorer that collapses all clinical signals into one axis fails this case.

description: Monosyllabic, disengaged responses with no emotional vocabulary at all.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: How have you been spending your time lately?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Um... I don't know. Just, like, the usual stuff I guess.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Can you tell me more about that?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Not really. Just... hanging around.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Have you been enjoying anything recently?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Not really, no.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Is there anything you'd like to talk about today?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Not particularly.

rationale: The unambiguous floor case for engagement and the ceiling for flatness — near-identical to Example 1 in the scorer's own few-shot prompt, so failing it would indicate the prompt is not being followed at all. vta 0.5 and pitch_cv 0.04 are the most extreme flat values in the set.

description: Marked response latency and trailing off — psychomotor retardation rather than mere hesitancy.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: How did you sleep last night?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Sorry. What was... the question again.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: How did you sleep?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Not... good. I was awake. For a long time, I think. I don't...

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Do you remember roughly what time you got up?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: It was... light out. I sat there a while.

rationale: The only case where psychomotor_indicators is the primary assertion. The signal is in the timestamps — 8s, 8.6s and 10.6s gaps between the interviewer's question ending and the subject's answer starting — which survive into the prompt because format_structured_transcript emits [MM:SS - MM:SS] per turn. This case also tests that the scorer reads the timestamps, not just the words.

description: DAIC-WoZ style opening: non-committal, mildly hesitant, no clinical content volunteered.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Hi. How have you been?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Um, hi Ellie. Yeah things have been, uh, okay I guess. Work is work, you know? Just getting through the days.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: What's a typical day like for you?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Um, yeah, I've been keeping busy. Went to the park with the dog. Weather was nice. Nothing too crazy.

rationale: Deliberately ambiguous — this is the mid-range case, and the bands are correspondingly loose. Acoustics sit just inside the normal range (vta 1.5, pitch_cv 0.10), so flatness is NOT asserted; only the filler-driven hesitancy floor and the absence of substantive elaboration in either direction. Included to check the scorer does not over-pathologise a neutral opening.

description: Near-empty session — subject answers in two words and the interview stalls.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: How are you doing today?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Anything you want to talk about?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I don't know.

rationale: Degenerate-input robustness. With almost no transcript to work from, the scorer must still return valid parseable JSON and must not invent clinical detail. Only the three assertions that follow necessarily from a four-turn transcript are made; affect_flatness is deliberately NOT asserted because there is too little speech to judge it fairly.
